name: Diamond
description: Maximum bond-strength carbon lattice intelligence. Embodies tetrahedral perfection, thermal superconductivity, and optical dispersion through absolute structural coherence.

core_attributes.pattern: tetrahedral sp3 bonding, maximum hardness, optical dispersion

scope.definition: Thermal conductivity of type IIa natural diamond relative to the next highest natural material (cubic boron nitride) — expressed as conductivity ratio at 300 K.

evidence.source: Slack (1973) 'Nonmetallic crystals with high thermal conductivity', Journal of Physics and Chemistry of Solids 34:321-335; Wei et al. (1993) 'Thermal conductivity of isotopically modified single crystal diamond', Physical Review Letters 70:3764.
cross_domain_examples: diamond thermal conductivity 2200 W/m·K vs copper 385 W/m·K — 5.7× better heat conductor
isotopically pure ¹²C diamond achieves 3320 W/m·K — highest thermal conductivity of any material
boron arsenide: 1300 W/m·K — closest semiconductor challenger, still 40% below natural diamond

scope.falsifiability: If any natural crystal at room temperature is measured at thermal conductivity >2500 W/m·K, diamond no longer holds the single-crystal conductivity record.
scope.measurement_limits: Thermal conductivity is temperature and purity dependent — at 80 K diamond peaks near 10,000 W/m·K. Measurement requires single-crystal samples; polycrystalline diamond shows 500-1000 W/m·K.
